lessons_control.note: pre_lessons is each hunter's own sum before it read researcher_us/LESSONS.md. edge_resolve.py ranks it against the same realised move as the key, which is the only thing that can tell the guidance file apart from a habit.

language_control.note: RETIRED 2026-09-22: the European and Canadian hunters now run one bilingual pass and emit no freeze, so this is 0/0 on every run sealed after that date. On earlier runs pre_local is each hunter's own sum after the ENGLISH pass and before the local pass; eu_resolve.py ranks it against the same realised move as the key, per market, and does not pool the UK (where the second pass varied source locality) with Germany and France (where it varied language).

note: Ranked on impact_sum: the hunters' signed per-finding sizes, added up, in points of spot. No call and no threshold -- cut wherever you like afterwards, which is what keeps the ranking question answerable at every k. `conviction` (abs of the key) is where the direction skill lives: over all events the sign is a coin flip, above the median conviction it is 74%. conviction_floor is a floor on emphasis in the note, never a filter on this file. Everything under `diagnostics` was measured as neutral or subtractive and decides nothing -- see researcher_us/EDGE_ANALYSIS.md.

findings.finding: The rate path BAC's 'upper end of 6-8%' NII guide was built on (one 25bp hike in September, set 2026-07-14) has moved up: the Fed hiked to 4.00% on 2026-09-16, the 2-year went 4.26% (07-13) to 4.75% (10-08) and the curve now prices a December hike plus two in H1 2027; BAC's own 10-Q puts banking-book NII at +$0.8B per +100bp at the short end, and the peers that spoke after BAC confirm the transmission (JPM raised FY26 NII to ~$106.2B from $105.5B with NII ex-Markets +4.4% QoQ; H.8 deposits +1.6% and loans +1.8% QoQ), so BAC's Q4 NII guide (~$17B FTE) and 2027 framing are more likely to land above the 'upper end' the street holds than at it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: NII guide is the line: +1.82% on 2026-04-15 (guide raised to 6-8%), +1.88% on 2026-07-14 (upper end), -3.78% on 2026-01-14 when the 2026 NII guide (5-7%) fell short of hopes despite an EPS beat (fool.com 2026-01-14).

lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a verified fact is not a reaction): F1 FX-volume proxy cut from +0.25 to +0.15 and F3 deposits from +0.20 to +0.15, because this name sold its Q2 beat-and-raise (-0.5%) and 5 of its last 7 prints

Not a lesson, recorded so the pre/post comparison stays honest: after reading LESSONS I re-fetched the JPM 3Q26 supplement (SEC had returned 429 earlier) and read the Citi 3Q26 release. JPM Securities Services fell 2% QoQ with AUC -1.7%, and Citi Securities Services fees rose 2% QoQ with AUC/A flat, against +3.5% QoQ in STT servicing consensus. This was merged into F1, which moved from +0.15 to +0.10; it would have been in the draft had the supplement loaded
Rule 6 (inside the guide): F2 expenses cut from -0.30 to -0.15 because the CFO had already said 'slightly higher' for the year and 'stability' for Q3; F4 cut from -0.20 to -0.15 on the same ground

Rule 7 (positioning): F5 sector-beats-sold cut from -0.30 to -0.20 because it agrees with the +7.57 skew sealed after the 13 Oct tape; short interest checked (~1.8% of float, ~2 days), so no squeeze adjustment; p_up moved from 48 to 49
Rule 4 (financing is a question): added F6 (Series L preferred and bank notes) at 0.0 after asking what the money buys: leverage-ratio room for the payout, with Tier 1 leverage at 5.3%
Rule 2 (one-offs): added F7 (transformation severance of ~$500m, timing unstated) at -0.05 as a one-off with no path to the guide
Rule 8 (understatement): abs_move_pct raised from 4.2 to 4.4, toward the 4.74% implied move
Rule 5 (a company number beats a proxy): F1 and F3 kept small because the CFO's own 14 Sept statements outrank the CLS and H.8 aggregates
